label: Suggestive Search
title: Suggestive Search
summary: Use a Suggestive Search to let people type and pick one item from a known list, such as their bank, with matches shown as they type.
corePrinciple: Type a little, then pick the right one.

sizing.title: Full width, with a floating list
sizing.description: Suggestive Search fills its container. The label is 17 px tall with 8 px to a 47 px field. The list opens 6 px below the field with 44 px rows, floats over what follows, and scrolls after 240 px.

content.title: Name the value, hint the search
content.description: Label the field with what it holds, such as “Bank name”, and use the placeholder for a search hint. Keep options short and unique, write the no-match message as what happened, and make errors say how to fix the pick.

sources.title: Use the public Suggestive Search contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (23 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Suggestive search has Idle, Open, and Active variants. The package bolds the typed text where Figma greys it, uses a grey placeholder, and marks the chosen row with a grey fill and a 16 px check (Figma: white with a 20 px check). On the web the field is a combobox: the arrow keys move through the suggestions, Enter picks one, Escape closes the list, and focus stays in the field after a pick. Each suggestion is announced by its label, and required and error are announced, with the message tied to the field. The published Storybook predates this build.
